cards.question: What is the Contingency Fund of the State?
cards.tip: The Contingency Fund is Part II of the State accounts. The Legislature set it up under Article 267(2).
cards.answer: The Contingency Fund is Part II of the State accounts. The Legislature set it up under Article 267(2).

quotes.text: In Part II of the accounts, the transactions connected with the Contingency Fund, established by the State Legislature under Article 267 (2) of the Constitution, are recorded.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Part II of Government accounts

cards.question: What is the treasury balance?
cards.tip: The treasury balance is the Government's cash in the treasury. Payments go out of it. Receipts come into it.
cards.answer: The treasury balance is the Government's cash in the treasury. Payments go out of it. Receipts come into it.

quotes.text: The moneys held in a treasury as part of the Government’s cash balance form the treasury balance, from which Government disbursements are made and into which Government receipts are paid.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Note 1 - Treasury balance and currency chest balance

cards.question: A new Treasury Officer takes charge. What must he do first?
cards.tip: He checks the cash balance before taking charge. He reports it to the Accountant General in Form T.R.1.
cards.answer: He checks the cash balance before taking charge. He reports it to the Accountant General in Form T.R.1.

quotes.text: Whenever the Treasury Officer hands over charge otherwise than temporarily, the relieving government servant shall, before taking charge, verify the cash balance in the district treasury in the manner prescribed in Rule 144 of part IV of these rules and report the result of his verification to the Accountant General with a certificate in Form T.R.1.
quotes.ref: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 52(a)

cards.question: Who must certify a treasury strong-room?
cards.tip: A PWD officer of Executive Engineer rank or above must certify it is secure and fit.
cards.answer: A PWD officer of Executive Engineer rank or above must certify it is secure and fit.

quotes.text: No place should be used as a strong-room, unless an officer of the Public Works Department not lower in rank than an Executive Engineer has certified that it is secure and fit for use as a strong room.
quotes.ref: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(a) Treasury strong room

cards.question: In which form is the Anamath Balance Register kept?
cards.tip: Form T.R.19. The treasurer keeps it.
cards.answer: Form T.R.19. The treasurer keeps it.

quotes.text: The treasurer shall maintain an Anamath Balance Register in Form T.R. 19 for recording these Anamath transactions and a separate column shall be provided for each class of items concerned.

cards.question: A cheque you issued is lost. What do you do?
cards.tip: Report it to the Treasury Officer at once. Ask him to stop payment.
cards.answer: Report it to the Treasury Officer at once. Ask him to stop payment.

quotes.text: When a drawing officer receives a report that a cheque drawn by him has been lost, he shall at once report the fact to the Treasury Officer and request him to stop payment of the cheques.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Rule 250 Lost cheques

cards.question: Can an earnest money deposit be repaid in part?
cards.tip: No. Earnest money deposit is never repaid in part.
cards.answer: No. Earnest money deposit is never repaid in part.

quotes.text: An earnest money deposit shall never be repaid in part.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, rule on repayment of deposits (earnest money deposit)

cards.question: Revenue is collected in one district for another. Where is it credited?
cards.tip: In the treasury account of the receiving district, under the proper head.
cards.answer: In the treasury account of the receiving district, under the proper head.

quotes.text: Revenue collected in one district on account of another should be credited in the treasury account of the receiving district under the appropriate head of account and the fact intimated to the appropriate departmental officer in the district concerned.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 8(7)(iii) Maintenance of proper accounts

cards.question: In which form is the Register of Increments kept?
cards.tip: Form 9A. The drawing officer keeps it.
cards.answer: Form 9A. The drawing officer keeps it.

quotes.text: A ‘Register of Increments’ will be maintained by the drawing officer, in Form 9 A in which the authorisation of increments will be recorded by him with corresponding entries in the Service Book.
quotes.ref: Kerala Financial Code Vol I, Article 78 (Drawal of an increment in pay)

cards.question: How long is an endorsement on a contingent bill valid?
cards.tip: Three months from the date of issue.
cards.answer: Three months from the date of issue.

quotes.text: No endorsement on a contingent bill remains valid for longer than three months counting from the date of issue.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 112(c) Endorsement of Contingent Bills in favour of private parties

cards.question: In which form is the register of immovable property kept?
cards.tip: Form 23. One register for buildings and land. One for roads, bridges and culverts.
cards.answer: Form 23. One register for buildings and land. One for roads, bridges and culverts.

quotes.text: The permanent registers, one for buildings and lands and the other for roads, bridges and culverts, will be maintained in Form 23 (I and II) by all Officers to show the assets of Government in the form of immovable properties under their charge.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 170 Maintenance of register of immovable properties

cards.question: Which register records Accountant General's audit objections?
cards.tip: A register in Form 4, kept in each office.
cards.answer: A register in Form 4, kept in each office.

quotes.text: A register should be maintained in each office in Form 4 for recording the objections communicated by the Accountant General.

cards.question: What is a permanent advance?
cards.tip: An advance to pay urgent bills before drawing them. Keep it to what is absolutely essential.
cards.answer: An advance to pay urgent bills before drawing them. Keep it to what is absolutely essential.

quotes.text: To enable him to make disbursements of this kind before drawing the necessary bills, a Government servant may be granted a permanent advance the amount of which should be limited to what is absolutely essential to meet his ordinary requirements.

cards.question: Is living in Government quarters you must occupy enough to claim compensation for theft loss?
cards.tip: No. It is not, by itself, a ground for compensation.
cards.answer: No. It is not, by itself, a ground for compensation.

quotes.text: The mere fact that at the time of the accident, the Government servant is technically on duty or is living in Government quarters in which he is bound to reside for the performance of his duties will not be considered as a sufficient ground for the grant of compensation.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 231(1)(c) Compensation for loss of property

cards.question: What are original works?
cards.tip: All new construction, plus additions and alterations to existing works.
cards.answer: All new construction, plus additions and alterations to existing works.

quotes.text: Original works include all new construction, whether of entirely new works or of additions and alterations to existing works, reconstruction of entire structures necessitated by wear and tear or by damage due to some calamity and all repairs to newly purchased or previously abandoned buildings required to make them usable.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 164 Classification of works

cards.question: What is a revised estimate?
cards.tip: An estimate made during the year. It uses actual figures so far, plus expected figures for the rest.
cards.answer: An estimate made during the year. It uses actual figures so far, plus expected figures for the rest.

quotes.text: Revised estimate is an estimate of the probable revenue and expenditure of the current financial year under the various heads, framed during the course of the year, based on the actual transactions so far recorded and the anticipation for the rest of the year.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Revised Estimate (Chapter II / para 20)

cards.question: Excess spending is found after the year ends. How is it treated?
cards.tip: Always as an irregularity.
cards.answer: Always as an irregularity.

quotes.text: As such, excess expenditure which comes to notice after the expiry of the financial year is always looked upon as an irregularity.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Para 97(1) Excess Grant

cards.question: Which register do disbursing officers keep for spending and liabilities?
cards.tip: A register in Form KBM 12.
cards.answer: A register in Form KBM 12.

quotes.text: each disbursing Officer should maintain a register of expenditure and liabilities, in Form KBM 12.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Para 70(1) Disbursing Officers

cards.question: Is a medical certificate needed for leave right after maternity leave?
cards.tip: Not for leave up to 60 days in continuation of maternity leave.
cards.answer: Not for leave up to 60 days in continuation of maternity leave.

quotes.text: Provided that no medical certificate shall be necessary for grant of any leave for a period not exceeding sixty days in continuation of maternity leave.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 102 (Maternity leave combined with other leave), proviso

cards.question: You are on leave and get suspended. What happens to the leave?
cards.tip: The leave is cancelled for the suspension period. You get subsistence allowance.
cards.answer: The leave is cancelled for the suspension period. You get subsistence allowance.

quotes.text: In the case of an Officer on leave with allowances, the orders of suspension shall have the effect of cancelling the leave for the period of suspension. He shall be entitled to subsistence allowance.

cards.question: Can a District Collector tour the adjoining districts of a neighbouring State?
cards.tip: Yes. Heads of Departments and District Collectors can approve such tours in the public interest.
cards.answer: Yes. Heads of Departments and District Collectors can approve such tours in the public interest.

quotes.text: Note 2.- The Heads of Departments and District Collectors will be competent to undertake journeys outside the State in the adjoining districts of neighbouring States in public interest.
quotes.ref: KSR Vol I, Rule 47 Note 2 (Travelling Allowances, Journeys on Tour)

cards.question: Is spending on a temporary asset capital expenditure?
cards.tip: Ordinarily, no.
cards.answer: Ordinarily, no.

quotes.text: (3) Expenditure on a temporary asset cannot ordinarily be considered as expenditure of a capital nature.
quotes.ref: KAC Vol I, Art. 30-A(3) Capital and Revenue

cards.question: Which form is the muster roll?
cards.tip: K.P.W. Form 19.
cards.answer: K.P.W. Form 19.

quotes.text: Muster rolls should be prepared in K.P.W. Form 19 and dealt with in accordance with the following rules:—

cards.question: Can an officer claim leave as a matter of right?
cards.tip: Leave cannot be claimed as a right. The sanctioning authority may refuse or revoke any leave when public service needs it.
cards.answer: Leave cannot be claimed as a right. The sanctioning authority may refuse or revoke any leave when public service needs it.

quotes.text: Leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right. When the exigencies of the public service so require, discretion to refuse or revoke leave of any description is reserved to the authority empowered to grant it.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 65 Leave not a right

cards.question: Can the sanctioning authority change the nature of leave applied for?
cards.tip: No. The authority may refuse or revoke the leave applied for, but cannot alter its nature.
cards.answer: No. The authority may refuse or revoke the leave applied for, but cannot alter its nature.

quotes.text: it is open to the sanctioning authority to refuse or revoke the leave due and applied for, it is not open to him to alter the nature of such leave.

cards.question: When does leave ordinarily begin and end?
cards.tip: Leave begins on the day charge is transferred and ends on the day before charge is resumed.
cards.answer: Leave begins on the day charge is transferred and ends on the day before charge is resumed.

quotes.text: Leave ordinarily begins on the day on which transfer of charge is effected and ends on the day preceding that on which charge is resumed.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 66 Beginning of leave

cards.question: If holidays are prefixed to leave, from when does the leave take effect?
cards.tip: Leave takes effect from the first day after the holidays, unless the competent authority directs otherwise.
cards.answer: Leave takes effect from the first day after the holidays, unless the competent authority directs otherwise.

quotes.text: if holidays are prefixed to leave, the leave and any consequent
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 68(a) Holidays prefixed

cards.question: If holidays are affixed to leave, when is the leave treated as ended?
cards.tip: The leave is treated as ended on the day it would have ended had the holidays not been affixed.
cards.answer: The leave is treated as ended on the day it would have ended had the holidays not been affixed.

quotes.text: if holidays are affixed to leave, the leave is treated as having terminated on, and any consequent re-arrangement of pay and allowances takes effect from, the day on which the leave would have ended, if holidays had not been affixed.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 68(b) Holidays affixed

cards.question: Who may allow an officer on leave to take up other employment?
cards.tip: An officer on leave needs previous sanction of the authority empowered to fill his post before taking service or employment.
cards.answer: An officer on leave needs previous sanction of the authority empowered to fill his post before taking service or employment.

quotes.text: An officer on leave may not take any service or accept any employment without obtaining the previous sanction of the authority empowered to fill up the post held by him.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 69 Employment during leave

cards.question: If an officer is recalled from leave, when is he treated as on duty?
cards.tip: If return is compulsory, he is on duty from the day he starts for the station, with leave salary only until he joins.
cards.answer: If return is compulsory, he is on duty from the day he starts for the station, with leave salary only until he joins.

quotes.text: if it is compulsory he is entitled to be treated as on duty from the date on which he starts for the station to which he is ordered
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 70 Recall from leave

cards.question: Can an officer on leave return to duty before the leave ends?
cards.tip: Not unless the authority which granted the leave permits it.
cards.answer: Not unless the authority which granted the leave permits it.

quotes.text: An officer on leave may not return to duty before the expiry of the period of leave granted to him, unless he is permitted to do so by the authority which granted him leave.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 72(1) Return before expiry

cards.question: Can an officer on leave preparatory to retirement withdraw his request and return?
cards.tip: No, unless the authority empowered to appoint him consents.
cards.answer: No, unless the authority empowered to appoint him consents.

quotes.text: an officer on leave preparatory to retirement shall be precluded from withdrawing his request for permission to retire and from returning to duty, save with the consent of the authority empowered to appoint him.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 72(2) Leave preparatory to retirement

cards.question: Is formal cancellation needed when an officer returns before leave ends?
cards.tip: No formal cancellation is needed. Audit Officer cancels for gazetted officers; Head of office for non-gazetted.
cards.answer: No formal cancellation is needed. Audit Officer cancels for gazetted officers; Head of office for non-gazetted.

quotes.text: No formal cancellation of the unexpired portion of leave is necessary when an officer returns to duty before the expiry of his leave. The cancellation will be effected by the Audit Officer in the case of Gazetted Officers and by the Head of office in the case of non- gazetted officers.

cards.question: Can any kind of leave be combined with another kind?
cards.tip: Yes, any leave may be combined with or follow any other leave, except leave under certain Appendices.
cards.answer: Yes, any leave may be combined with or follow any other leave, except leave under certain Appendices.

quotes.text: kind of leave under these rules may be granted in combination with or in continuation of any other kind of leave except leave under Appendices
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 73 Combination of leave

cards.question: On what date is eligibility for leave determined?
cards.tip: Eligibility is decided on the date the officer proceeds on leave.
cards.answer: Eligibility is decided on the date the officer proceeds on leave.

quotes.text: The eligibility for leave is determined with reference to the eligibility on the date on which an officer proceeds on leave.

cards.question: What is the limit on earned leave plus commuted leave taken together?
cards.tip: The combination of earned leave and commuted leave is limited to 240 days.
cards.answer: The combination of earned leave and commuted leave is limited to 240 days.

quotes.text: The combination of earned leave and commuted leave will be limited to 240 days.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 74 Vacation and leave

cards.question: Is there a limit on half-pay leave taken at a time?
cards.tip: No limit on half-pay leave at a time on medical certificate or private affairs, even before retirement.
cards.answer: No limit on half-pay leave at a time on medical certificate or private affairs, even before retirement.

quotes.text: There will be no limit on the half-pay leave that can be availed of at a time on medical certificate or private affairs. This will apply even when such leave is taken preparatory to retirement.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 74 Half-pay leave limit

cards.question: Can leave be granted beyond the date of compulsory retirement?
cards.tip: No leave can be granted beyond the date on which an officer must compulsorily retire.
cards.answer: No leave can be granted beyond the date on which an officer must compulsorily retire.

quotes.text: No leave shall be granted beyond the date on which an officer must compulsorily retire
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 75 Leave beyond retirement

cards.question: Can leave be retrospectively commuted into another kind?
cards.tip: Yes, into any other kind admissible when the original leave was granted. Earned leave cannot be commuted, with a stated exception.
cards.answer: Yes, into any other kind admissible when the original leave was granted. Earned leave cannot be commuted, with a stated exception.

quotes.text: Any leave granted under these rules may be retrospectively commuted into any other kind of leave admissible to the officer at the time the original leave was granted
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 76 Retrospective commutation

cards.question: What is the time limit for retrospective commutation of leave?
cards.tip: No commutation of leave is allowed after one year from the date of sanction of leave.
cards.answer: No commutation of leave is allowed after one year from the date of sanction of leave.

quotes.text: no commutation of leave shall be permitted on expiry of one year from the date of sanction of leave.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 76 second proviso / Rule 89(i)

cards.question: Can an officer claim retrospective commutation as a right?
cards.tip: No. The granting authority may commute it, but the officer cannot claim it as a matter of right.
cards.answer: No. The granting authority may commute it, but the officer cannot claim it as a matter of right.

quotes.text: The authority which granted leave to an officer can commute it retrospectively into leave of a different kind which may be admissible but the officer concerned cannot claim it as a matter of right
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 89(i) Commutation with retrospective effect

cards.question: What follows automatically when leave is commuted into another kind?
cards.tip: Arrears of leave salary are drawn, or amounts overdrawn are recovered.
cards.answer: Arrears of leave salary are drawn, or amounts overdrawn are recovered.

quotes.text: Commutation of one kind of leave into another automatically carries with it the drawal of arrears of leave salary or recovery of amounts overdrawn.

cards.question: What does 'ordinary leave' include?
cards.tip: Ordinary leave means earned leave, half-pay leave, commuted leave, leave not due and leave without allowances.
cards.answer: Ordinary leave means earned leave, half-pay leave, commuted leave, leave not due and leave without allowances.

quotes.text: ‘Ordinary leave’ includes earned leave, half-pay leave, commuted leave, leave not due and leave without allowances.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 77(i) Ordinary leave

cards.question: What does 'special leave' include?
cards.tip: Special leave includes disability leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, child adoption leave and hospital leave.
cards.answer: Special leave includes disability leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, child adoption leave and hospital leave.

quotes.text: ‘Special leave’ includes disability leave, maternity leave, *paternity leave, †child adoption leave and hospital leave.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 77(ii) Special leave

cards.question: What is 'half-pay leave' earned in respect of?
cards.tip: Half-pay leave is leave earned in respect of completed years of service.
cards.answer: Half-pay leave is leave earned in respect of completed years of service.

quotes.text: ‘Half-pay leave’ means leave earned in respect of completed years of service.

cards.question: Who is an 'officer in permanent employ'?
cards.tip: One who holds a permanent post substantively, or holds a lien (or would hold it but for suspension) on a permanent post.
cards.answer: One who holds a permanent post substantively, or holds a lien (or would hold it but for suspension) on a permanent post.

quotes.text: ‘Officer in permanent employ’ means an officer who holds substantively a permanent post or who holds a lien on a permanent post or who would hold a lien on a permanent post had the lien not been suspended.

cards.question: At what rate is earned leave earned by a permanent officer?
cards.tip: One-eleventh of the period spent on duty.
cards.answer: One-eleventh of the period spent on duty.

quotes.text: The earned leave admissible to an officer in permanent employ is one-eleventh of the period spent on duty
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 78 Earned leave rate

cards.question: What is the maximum accumulation of earned leave?
cards.tip: Earned leave stops being earned when the earned leave due reaches 300 days.
cards.answer: Earned leave stops being earned when the earned leave due reaches 300 days.

quotes.text: he will cease to earn such leave when the earned leave due amounts *300 days.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 78 Accumulation limit

cards.question: What is the maximum earned leave granted at a time?
cards.tip: 180 days at a time.
cards.answer: 180 days at a time.

quotes.text: the maximum earned leave that may be granted at a time to an officer shall be # 180 days.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 79 Maximum at a time

cards.question: What is the maximum earned leave at a time for leave preparatory to retirement?
cards.tip: 300 days at a time.
cards.answer: 300 days at a time.

quotes.text: In the case of an officer applying for leave preparatory to retirement, the maximum earned leave that may be granted at a time shall be *300 days.

cards.question: Is earned leave admissible to a vacation department officer who takes the full vacation?
cards.tip: No, no earned leave for duty in a year in which he avails himself of the full vacation.
cards.answer: No, no earned leave for duty in a year in which he avails himself of the full vacation.

quotes.text: Earned leave is not admissible to an officer in permanent employ serving in a vacation department in respect of duty performed in any year in which he avails himself of the full vacation.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 80 Vacation department

cards.question: How much earned leave does a vacation department officer get if vacation is not fully taken?
cards.tip: Such proportion of 30 days as the vacation days not taken bear to the full vacation.
cards.answer: Such proportion of 30 days as the vacation days not taken bear to the full vacation.

quotes.text: is such proportion of 30 days as the number of days of vacation not taken bears to the full vacation.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 81 Vacation not fully availed

cards.question: What does 'year' mean for a vacation department officer?
cards.tip: Not a calendar year, but twelve months of actual duty in a vacation department.
cards.answer: Not a calendar year, but twelve months of actual duty in a vacation department.

quotes.text: The term “Year” should be interpreted to mean, not a calendar year in which duty is performed, but twelve months of actual duty in a vacation department.

cards.question: What is the earned leave rate in the first year for an officer not in permanent employ?
cards.tip: 1/22 of the period spent on duty in the first year.
cards.answer: 1/22 of the period spent on duty in the first year.

quotes.text: in respect of the first year of service the earned leave admissible is 1/22 of the period spent on duty
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 86 Non-permanent officer

cards.question: When fractions arise on a change in the rate of earning leave, how are they rounded?
cards.tip: Fractions below half are ignored; half or more is counted as a day.
cards.answer: Fractions below half are ignored; half or more is counted as a day.

quotes.text: fraction below half should be ignored and that of half and more should be reckoned as a day.

cards.question: After how many years of continuous service is a non-permanent officer eligible for commuted leave, earned leave and LWA?
cards.tip: After three years of continuous service, as if he held the post substantively.
cards.answer: After three years of continuous service, as if he held the post substantively.

quotes.text: an officer not in permanent employ who has completed three years of continuos service shall be eligible for (i) commutted leave, (ii) earned leave and (iii) leave

cards.question: How many days of half-pay leave per completed year of service?
cards.tip: 20 days for each completed year of service.
cards.answer: 20 days for each completed year of service.

quotes.text: The half-pay leave admissible to an officer in permanent employ in respect of each completed year of service is 20 days.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 83 Half-pay leave

cards.question: For what reasons can half-pay leave be availed?
cards.tip: On private affairs or on medical certificate.
cards.answer: On private affairs or on medical certificate.

quotes.text: Half-pay leave as provided in Rule 83 may be availed of on private affairs or on medical certificate.

cards.question: How much commuted leave can be granted?
cards.tip: Not more than half the half-pay leave due.
cards.answer: Not more than half the half-pay leave due.

quotes.text: Commuted leave not exceeding half the amount of half-pay leave due may be granted to an officer in permanent employ.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 84 Commuted leave

cards.question: How much half-pay leave is debited when commuted leave is granted?
cards.tip: Twice the commuted leave is debited against half-pay leave due.
cards.answer: Twice the commuted leave is debited against half-pay leave due.

quotes.text: When Commuted Leave is granted twice the amount of such leave shall be debited against the half-pay leave due.

cards.question: What is the maximum leave not due in entire service?
cards.tip: Not exceeding 360 days in entire service.
cards.answer: Not exceeding 360 days in entire service.

quotes.text: leave not due may be granted to an officer in permanent employ for a period not exceeding 360 days during his entire service
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 85 Leave not due

cards.question: What are the limits on leave not due taken otherwise than on medical certificate?
cards.tip: Not more than 90 days at a time and 180 days in all.
cards.answer: Not more than 90 days at a time and 180 days in all.

quotes.text: not more than 90 days at a time and 180 days in all may be otherwise than on medical certificate.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 85 Leave not due

cards.question: Against what is leave not due debited?
cards.tip: It is debited against half-pay leave the officer earns subsequently.
cards.answer: It is debited against half-pay leave the officer earns subsequently.

quotes.text: This will be debited against half-pay leave which the officer earns subsequently.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 85 Leave not due

cards.question: When should leave not due be granted?
cards.tip: Only when no other leave with allowance is available, and there is reasonable prospect of return and earning equal half-pay leave.
cards.answer: Only when no other leave with allowance is available, and there is reasonable prospect of return and earning equal half-pay leave.

quotes.text: only when no other leave with allowance is available at credit of the officer and if the authority empowered to sanction leave] is satisfied that there is a reasonable prospect of the officer returning to duty on the expiry of the leave and earning an equal amount of half pay leave thereafter.

cards.question: What happens to leave not due if the officer applies for voluntary retirement and it is granted?
cards.tip: The leave not due is cancelled.
cards.answer: The leave not due is cancelled.

quotes.text: the leave not due shall, if the permission is granted, be cancelled.

cards.question: If an officer fails to earn leave not due by later duty, is it cancelled?
cards.tip: No. Subject to his wishes, it stands, even if he fails to earn it.
cards.answer: No. Subject to his wishes, it stands, even if he fails to earn it.

quotes.text: leave not due when granted should in all cases (subject to the officer’s wishes) be allowed to stand, including cases in which the officer fails to earn it by subsequent duty.

cards.question: What is leave salary on earned leave?
cards.tip: Full duty pay, dearness allowance on it, and admissible compensatory allowances.
cards.answer: Full duty pay, dearness allowance on it, and admissible compensatory allowances.

quotes.text: An officer on earned leave is entitled to leave salary equal to,- (i) full (duty) pay i.e., pay admissible had he been on duty during the period of leave;
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 92(i) Leave salary on earned leave

cards.question: What is leave salary on half pay leave or leave not due?
cards.tip: Half of duty pay, plus dearness allowance on that half.
cards.answer: Half of duty pay, plus dearness allowance on that half.

quotes.text: An officer on half pay leave or leave not due is entitled to leave salary equal to,- (i) half of duty pay, i e., half of the pay admissible had he been on duty during the period of leave;

cards.question: What is leave salary on commuted leave?
cards.tip: Twice the amount of half pay leave salary (twice the pay under Rule 93(i)).
cards.answer: Twice the amount of half pay leave salary (twice the pay under Rule 93(i)).

quotes.text: An officer on commuted leave is entitled to leave salary equal to twice the amount of the pay admissible under clause (i) of Rule 93
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 94 Commuted leave salary

cards.question: Is leave salary payable on leave without allowances?
cards.tip: No, an officer on leave without allowances gets no leave salary.
cards.answer: No, an officer on leave without allowances gets no leave salary.

quotes.text: An officer on leave without allowances is not entitled to any leave salary.

cards.question: For how long are HRA, CCA and Hill Tract Allowance paid during leave with allowances?

cards.question: What are original works?

cards.answer: All new construction, additions and alterations, reconstruction of entire structures after wear or calamity, and repairs to newly purchased or abandoned buildings to make them usable.

cards.answer: Operations to keep existing properties in satisfactory state and make good wear and tear damage when complete reconstruction is not necessary.

cards.answer: As ordinary repairs and special repairs.

cards.answer: The order of a competent authority sanctioning a properly detailed estimate of cost of a construction or repair work to be done by the PWD.
